default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1118.title: Qstick zero-line cross follow
E-1118.hypothesis: The average bar body (close minus open) over a window turning positive means buyers have been winning the inside of the bars, not just the close; the aggressor side keeps pushing for a few more minutes.

E-1119.title: TRIX zero-line cross follow
E-1119.hypothesis: A triple-smoothed EMA turning up filters out noise; when even that slow line turns, the trend change is real and later participants chase it.

E-1120.title: DeMarker exit from extreme, follow
E-1120.hypothesis: DeMarker compares new highs with new lows bar by bar; leaving the exhausted zone (below lo or above 1-lo) shows the pressure that dominated has stopped, so trade the turn.

E-1121.title: Dual Thrust open-trigger break
E-1121.hypothesis: The range of the last sessions sets how far the day must travel from its open to be a trending day; a close beyond open +/- k of that range attracts breakout orders and follows.

E-1122.title: Positive-volume-index trend cross follow
E-1122.hypothesis: Price moves on rising volume are made by the crowd; when that crowd-driven cumulative move crosses its own average, the crowd changes direction and later followers continue.

E-1123.title: EMA ribbon stack onset
E-1123.hypothesis: Three EMAs of doubling length lining up in order marks every horizon agreeing on direction for the first time; slower holders then join.

E-1124.title: Awesome oscillator zero cross
E-1124.hypothesis: The 5-bar mean of the median price crossing a longer mean shows momentum overtaking the slower average of the market's fair price; follow it.

E-1125.title: VWAP-side dominance dip
E-1125.hypothesis: When price spent nearly the whole window on one side of VWAP, institutional benchmark buyers or sellers are in control; a touch of VWAP that closes back on that side is where they add.

E-1126.title: Session-drift t-stat cross follow
E-1126.hypothesis: The day's cumulative return divided by its own realised noise is a signal-to-noise ratio; when it crosses a high level the drift is statistically distinct from a random walk and tends to persist.

E-1127.title: Mean-median price skew flip follow
E-1127.hypothesis: The mean of closes sitting above their median means the recent window has a tail of high prints not yet in the middle of the distribution; price drifts toward the tail.
